chief_complaint: Increasing shortness of breath, especially with exertion, and swelling in my ankles.
doctor_notes: Patient presents with worsening dyspnea and peripheral edema, consistent with a CHF exacerbation. BP elevated, HR within normal limits. Labs show elevated BNP, consistent with fluid overload. Glycemic control suboptimal. Plan to adjust diuretic regimen and monitor fluid balance. Discussed importance of medication adherence and dietary modifications.

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Doctor, I've been feeling so tired and my legs are really swollen lately. It's hard to catch my breath even when I'm just walking to the kitchen.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: Hello Eleanor. I see. You mentioned your breathing has been worse. Have you noticed any changes in your cough or any chest pain?

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: No chest pain, thankfully. My cough is a little worse at night sometimes.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: And how have you been with your medications and diet? Have you been watching your salt intake?

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: I try my best, doctor, but sometimes it's hard. I haven't been as good about it lately.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: I understand. We'll adjust your furosemide to help with the fluid, but it's crucial we work together on managing your salt and fluid intake. We'll also increase your spironolactone. I want you to weigh yourself daily and keep a log.
